title: Chapter 18
content:
"Go on. Have a drag."

Kang Il-hyun held out the lit cigarette between his fingers.

Jakyeong clamped his lips shut. Has he figured it out? If he has, how much does he know? And when the hell did he see my tattoo?

Though his eyes stayed locked onto the burning tip of the cigarette, a storm of calculations tore through his mind. He couldn't afford to jump to conclusions just yet.

Forcing a soft, fragile smile, he politely shook his head. "My lungs aren't very strong..."

"Liar."

Jakyeong waved an arm to swat away the drifting smoke, forcing a fit of dry, hacking coughs.

Il-hyun let out a low chuckle, pulled the cigarette back, and snubbed it out in the obsidian ashtray. Leaning back into the sofa, he crossed his arms, his gaze settling heavily on Jakyeong.

Dabbing his mouth with the back of his wrist, Jakyeong offered a few more delicate coughs while cautiously gauging the man's expression.

"Are you... going to tell my grandfather?"

Il-hyun said nothing.

Jakyeong’s face fell into an anxious, troubled frown. "Please don't. If he finds out I got a tattoo, he'll be furious..."

His voice shrank down to a meek, guilty murmur, perfectly mimicking a child terrified of being scolded by their parents.

Il-hyun reached for the cut-crystal tumbler beside him, tossed in a few ice cubes, and poured a measure of liquor. Amber liquid filled the glass halfway. Jakyeong watched him with bated breath, bracing for whatever verdict might slip past those lips.

Il-hyun took a slow, silent sip. "It's hardly a crime."

"You know how he is, Director Kang..."

"True. The old man is a traditionalist. Stiff as a board."

The sharp clink of ice swirling against crystal sounded unnervingly loud in the quiet room. Jakyeong nodded submissively, letting his shoulders slump into a gloomy posture.

"You're right... He's excessively protective. Sometimes... it feels suffocating."

Il-hyun gently rotated the glass in his hand, offering no comment.

"Being able to hang out with guys my own age here in Korea was so much fun..." Jakyeong continued, weaving his cover story. "It felt like a little rebellion. Back in Hong Kong, I could never... I couldn't even dream of doing something like that..."

Jakyeong let his brows drop, painting a look of quiet misery across his face. His lips trembled slightly, and he let out a soft, defeated sigh. When a man was cornered by survival instincts, an Oscar-worthy performance practically materialized out of thin air. No matter how much Wang Han had drilled him on acting like a frail heir, pure adrenaline was proving far more effective.

"My father died like that... so I know why my grandfather is so obsessed with shielding me. But I'm an adult now. Earlier, when you said you had men tailing me without my knowledge... that was why I lashed out. Thinking that nothing was going to change from how I lived back in Hong Kong... it just made my chest tighten."

Jakyeong’s eyes flushed red with unshed tears, choking back his words.

Il-hyun drained the rest of his whiskey in one swallow. Jakyeong waited a beat, letting the silence hang before delivering the final apology.

"I'm sure you only did it out of the same concern my grandfather has... Losing my temper was reckless of me. I'm truly sorry."

Biting his lower lip, Jakyeong cast his eyes downward with a repentant expression.

An absolute, graveyard quiet fell over the room.

When Jakyeong finally dared to lift his gaze, he saw Il-hyun staring down at his smartphone, tapping away at a screen.

After winding me up like a top, this is what you do?

Glancing up from his screen, Il-hyun caught Jakyeong’s eye. "Excuse me. Pressing business."

"Of course..."

"Head on up and get some sleep."

Rising from the sofa, Il-hyun brought the phone to his ear, muttering something about a shipment deal as he disappeared into the inner bedroom.

Left alone in the parlor, Jakyeong stared dumbfounded at the closed door. What was all that? He’d worked up the tension, squeezed out actual tears, and put on the performance of a lifetime—only for the guy to brush it off like static.

Glaring at the bedroom door, Jakyeong pushed himself up from the couch. The sudden release of adrenaline left his knees feeling slightly rubbery.

As he stepped out into the hallway, the senior housekeeper approached, asking with a warm smile if she should prepare a late-night snack for him.

"No, thank you, ma'am. I'm quite alright."

"Why not? A young man your age ought to be eating constantly."

Jakyeong had aged out of that demographic a long time ago. Though he hated deceiving such a kind soul, he offered an apologetic, awkward chuckle and gently turned down her offer.

Seeing her always brought Wang Han’s grandmother to mind. When Jakyeong had first fled to China as a boy, he had lived with Wang Han’s family, which was where he met the old matriarch. The image of her sitting in the tiny courtyard, quietly knitting, remained vivid in his memory even years after her passing. She had cherished Jakyeong, offering gentle guidance and urging him to live a life full of good deeds.

She certainly never imagined that those "good deeds" would turn out to be contract killings.

Returning to his second-floor suite, Jakyeong locked himself inside the bathroom and finally let out a long, ragged breath. It was the only sanctuary in this entire fortified mansion where he could truly let down his guard.

Leaning against the sink, he replayed every beat of the conversation in his head. Il-hyun's words. His cadence. The look in his eyes.

When had he spotted the tattoo? Was it down in the basement vault when his shirt had gotten torn open during the scuffle? Had the bastard picked up on anything else? One day Il-hyun looked at him like a hawk sizing up an imposter, and the next he treated him like a coddled younger brother. It was impossible to pinpoint where the man stood.

Removing his horn-rimmed glasses, Jakyeong turned the tap and splashed cold water over his face repeatedly. Bracing both hands against the marble basin, he looked up to meet his reflection in the mirror. Droplets trailed down his chin, but the tension lingering in his sharp jawline refused to wash away.

Reaching into his pocket, he pulled out his encrypted phone and sat on the rim of the bathtub.

The line rang several times before Wang Han’s raspy voice answered.

[What's going on at this hour?]

"I need to ask you something."

[What's with that tone? Did something happen?]

"Find out who placed the contract on Kang Il-hyun."

Silence fell over the line.

In this line of work, when a contract came through a broker like Dmitri rather than directly from a client, asking about the employer's identity was strictly taboo. It was an unspoken golden rule of the underworld, and Jakyeong had never breached it in his entire career.

Sensing that the mission had gone sideways, Wang Han’s voice tightened.

[Did things blow up?]

"No. Not yet."

['Not yet'? What does that mean? Besides, Dmitri would never burn a client like that.]

"Tell him if he doesn't give up the name, I'm returning the deposit and walking away."

[Jakyeong.]

"I'm dead serious."

Wang Han didn't push further. He had been uneasy about the contract from day one, so he knew Jakyeong wouldn't make a demand like this without serious justification. But walking away mid-contract carried catastrophic risks. If word leaked that an assassin had broken protocol, the syndicate would demand blood—either in raw cash or in body parts.

[Fine. I'll get the name. That all you need?]

"Yeah. Thanks, Hyung. Talk soon."

Ending the call, Jakyeong slipped the phone back into his pocket and locked eyes with his reflection once more.

["And why someone who speaks with such polite deference... has the dead, predatory eyes of an underworld thug."]

Jakyeong clenched his jaw tight.

It sounded completely insane, but for a split second, a bizarre suspicion had crossed his mind: Could Kang Il-hyun be the one who ordered the hit on himself?

To an outsider, the idea was preposterous. Who in their right mind hired a hitman to put a bullet in their own brain?

Yet it wasn't entirely unheard of. Early in his career, Jakyeong had taken a contract from a famous Russian ballet dancer who was embroiled in a tormented affair with a powerful politician’s wife. Consumed by severe clinical depression over the realization that he could never truly have her, the dancer had hired Jakyeong to end his life.

His only condition: execute him publicly during a live performance while the woman sat in the audience with her husband, ensuring she would live with the horrific memory branded into her mind forever. The dancer died, and the sensational murder dominated the tabloids for weeks.

Later, the woman had made occasional appearances on television. Contrary to the dancer's dying wish, she looked radiant, smiling as she described her current life as the most blessed chapter of her existence.

Kang Il-hyun, however, was fundamentally different. He was not the type to sacrifice his own life for romance or theatrical vengeance. He was the kind of apex predator who leveraged lives to extort, dominate, and butcher.

Jakyeong wiped his damp face with a rough swipe of his sleeve. If only I could crack that bastard's skull open and see what's ticking inside.

Stepping out of his en-suite bathroom, Il-hyun towelled his damp hair dry and pulled on a pair of loose lounge pants.

Entering the parlor, he fed the pet reef sharks gliding inside the recessed aquarium, watching with satisfaction as their razor-sharp teeth tore into the raw meat. Amused by their feral efficiency, he grabbed two chilled cans of beer from the mini-fridge and returned to the master bedroom.

Sinking into the leather sofa, he popped a tab, taking a cold gulp as he picked up the remote control and aimed it at the wall-mounted screen.

With a click, the feed switched from the evening news to the estate’s closed-circuit surveillance matrix, dividing the monitor into dozens of high-definition camera feeds covering every inch of the grounds.

He tapped another button, pulling up the feed from the second-floor guest suite.

Jang Yi-an was lying on the bed, tossing and turning as if sleep were completely out of reach. Il-hyun took another swig of beer, his eyes glued to the display, occasionally letting out a dry, entertained chuckle as if watching a late-night comedy special.

On screen, the boy suddenly sat up.

Thinking he was heading for the restroom, Il-hyun watched as the youth casually pulled his button-down shirt over his head.

Il-hyun had already felt the lean muscle under that clothing during their scuffle, but seeing it bare revealed a frame that was remarkably toned—compact, powerful, and completely devoid of excess fat.

When the camera caught the dark ink coiling across the right shoulder, Il-hyun ran his tongue slowly over his lower lip.

"A snake, is it?"

He’d only caught a fleeting glimpse in the subterranean vault, but the high-res night vision finally revealed the full design: an open-mouthed viper poised to strike.

On screen, the boy shed his trousers, stripping down until he was wearing nothing but dark briefs before collapsing back onto the mattress. Il-hyun clicked his tongue in mild disappointment; the monochrome night-vision palette failed to capture the natural tone of the youth's skin.

Even stripped bare, Yi-an continued to toss and turn. He pulled the duvet up over his chest, kicked it off in frustration, and rolled over again. Up until yesterday, he had moved with careful restraint, conscious of the camera overhead; now that he believed his cover was cracked, he wasn't bothering to hide his restlessness.

Eventually, the thrashing subsided. The youth curled into a tight fetal ball beneath the sheets, finally surrendering to exhaustion.

Il-hyun crushed the empty aluminum can in his fist, picked up the remote, and switched off the display.

Click.

The room plunged into darkness, leaving only the faint blue ambient glow of the aquarium cutting through the shadows.
